lines.say: Once a year, millions of tiny lamps light up homes all over India. Why?
It's Diwali, the festival of lights! It's celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and some Buddhists.
For many Hindus, it remembers Prince Rama coming home after defeating an evil king. People lit lamps to welcome him back.
These little clay lamps are called diyas. The big idea: light wins over darkness, and good wins over evil.
Families clean their homes, draw colorful patterns called rangoli, share sweets, and set off fireworks.
Many also pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of good fortune.
Diwali lasts about five days, every autumn. Have you ever seen it? Tell me in the comments!
